author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T170438Z-856615
text:
Implemented.

Changes:

1. `MemoryBackend::query_objects::<Mailbox>` now honors filter+sort+paginate
   directly. Previously the default branch (memory.rs:588-604) collected all
   ids unfiltered/unsorted; now there's an early Mailbox dispatch to a new
   inherent helper `MemoryBackend::query_mailboxes` (memory.rs).

2. `handle_mailbox_query` (mailbox.rs) no longer fetches the full mailbox
   list and filters/sorts in-handler. The non-anchor path pushes
   limit/position directly to the backend. The anchor path follows the
   Email/query precedent: one full fetch (limit=None, position=0) to resolve
   the anchor index, then slice in-handler.

3. Fixed a latent bug in `MailboxFilterCondition.parent_id`: the doc
   claimed `Option<serde_json::Value>` with `#[serde(default)]` preserved
   the three-way absent/null/string distinction, but serde's default
   `Option<T>` Deserialize impl collapses JSON `null` to `None`. The
   original handler worked around this by peeking the raw JSON before
   deserialising. Now uses a custom `deserialize_with` that wraps the
   deserialised value in `Some(_)` whenever the field is present, so an
   explicit `null` becomes `Some(Value::Null)`. Three new round-trip
   tests in jmap-mail-types lock the semantics.

4. Updated `JmapBackend::query_objects` rustdoc to require production
   backends to honor filter/sort efficiently and to caution handlers
   against post-filtering / post-sorting.

5. Added two unit-level integration tests that call
   `backend.query_objects::<Mailbox>()` directly (no handler) to prove the
   storage-pushed contract for the reference impl.

Sibling-crate audit: no other extension-server crate has the same
handler-side bypass pattern. `chat/chat`, `contacts/card`,
`tasks/task`, `filenode/filenode`, `sharing/principal`,
`sharing/notification`, `calendars/event_notification`,
`tasks/task_notification` already use the generic `handle_query::<O>`
helper. `chat/message`, `chat/space`, `chat/contact`,
`chat/emoji` already call `query_objects` directly.
`calendars/event` uses a calendar-specific `query_calendar_events`
backend method for occurrence expansion. So no canonical-template
propagation is needed here.

Gates:
- cargo test --workspace: 113 test result lines, 0 failures
- cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo fmt --all: applied
- RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p jmap-mail-server -p jmap-mail-types -p jmap-server --no-deps: clean
  (a pre-existing rustdoc warning in jmap-calendars-client is filed as JMAP-pwng)
